coverage_notes: Rendered short-named, byte-identical PDF copy verified against the original SHA-256. Fingerprints refer to original input bytes. All 40 entries and seven CRA rows considered. All registered primary/secondary anchors on PDF pp.3,4,6,10,12 and material/method context on pp.2-3 visually inspected. Registry activities, brackets and result origins retained.
shared_qualifications: C1: All source potentials are reported vs NHE, although measured using SCE, and tests were at 25 C (PDF p.3). For comparison adopt the explicitly stated 25 C saturated-KCl convention E_SCE_vs_NHE=+0.241 V (Corrtest CS900 manufacturer, https://www.corrtestinstruments.com/en/02437.html). E_mV(SCE)=1000*E_V(NHE)-241. Source does not give its own numerical offset; comparison is conditional on this convention, not a reconstruction of the authors' calibration. Strict bounds keep their directions.

Fig.5 has two axes: NaCl activity below and concentration above. Activity 0.01, 0.08, 0.7 and 4.5 is linked to concentration 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 5 M by the displayed axes; activity is not assumed equal to molarity.
Nominal Al-4%Cu and Al-0.2%Cu analyses are measured as 4.07 and 0.27 wt.% Cu (PDF p.2). CRA uses nominal 4.0/0.2 wt.% values. The nominal/analytical distinction is retained.

Fig.6 EpI/EpII are expected phase thresholds, not independently measured bulk onsets. Table 1 reports strict potential-region limits, with mixed pitting/intergranular attack in the aged case. Candidates retain these differences and unresolved processing identities.
Table 2 >+3 V outcomes are strict no-pitting bounds. None is converted to an exact pitting potential or discarded solely because it is censored.
